common.points: a check-in is the point of its public catalog venue on the catalog's local plane (Catalog.xy, km, equirectangular at the study-area centre latitude)
common.data_boundaries: the public study area [0, W] x [0, H] km (Catalog.width_km, height_km) replaces every source's 'data boundaries' (the original dataset's bounding box), so grids and queries are public and identical for all releases
common.grid_cell_order: x-major, index = ix * g + iy (AdaTrace Grid.getCells, LDPTrace/RetraSyn GridMap.map[i][j] with i along x); a point on an interior cell edge goes to the higher cell (floor rule)
common.time: minutes since Monday 00:00 of the week in which the trail starts (trails.py); time of day = t mod 1440
common.size_rescaling: every source evaluated releases with as many trajectories as the original; counts compared across datasets (range queries, pattern supports, trajectory counts) multiply the release's counts by s = n_trails(reference) / n_trails(release)

reference.primary: real train split (the synthesizer's input: the 'original' dataset of every source)
reference.noise_floor: real test split evaluated against real train (eval_bench.py --reference)

common.rng: numpy.random.default_rng([seed, stream]) per query family; queries depend only on the study area, so every release of a dataset gets the same queries
common.log_base: natural log for every divergence (all source codes use numpy/scipy/Java natural log)

datasets.evaluation: every other dataset; scripts/eval_bench.py refuses to run on it unless frozen/benchmark_protocol_v1.sha256 matches the protocol files

metrics.name: ada_query_avre
metrics.statistic: average relative error of circular range queries; a query counts the trajectories that have a point or a segment within the circle
metrics.adaptation: centres uniform in the study area; radius = longer side / 3 (Query.java:40-43, the branch for datasets other than brinkhoff/taxi/geolife); Query.java:57 returns true for ANY trajectory with two identical consecutive points (a guard for its segment helper), we treat such a segment as a point; release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: ada_kendall_tau
metrics.statistic: Kendall tau between the per-cell numbers of grid trajectories passing through each cell (location coverage), AdaTrace's tie convention
metrics.adaptation: grid trajectories as AdaTrace (consecutive duplicate cells removed, a trail inside one cell becomes [c, c], non-adjacent cells joined by the diagonal-first route); pairs with tied real counts are skipped; when real counts differ and release counts tie, the pair is discordant if real_i > real_j and concordant if real_i < real_j (Evaluation.java:481-492), denominator n(n-1)/2 over all cells

metrics.name: ada_fp_f1
metrics.statistic: F1 between the top-100 frequent patterns (contiguous cell sub-sequences of size 2..8 of the grid trajectories, by number of occurrences) of the original and the release
metrics.adaptation: grid trajectories as ada_kendall_tau; ties in pattern support broken by pattern key (Java's order is hash-dependent); precision = hits / |release top-k|, recall = hits / |original top-k|; F1 = 0 when there is no hit

metrics.name: ada_fp_support_are
metrics.statistic: mean over the original's top-100 patterns of |support_orig - support_release| / support_orig
metrics.adaptation: release supports rescaled by s

metrics.name: ada_trip_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between the (start cell, end cell) distributions
metrics.adaptation: TripDistribution's Laplace noise of scale 1e-4 followed by rounding is the identity on counts and is omitted

metrics.name: ada_diameter_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between diameter distributions (largest distance between two points of a trajectory) over 20 buckets
metrics.adaptation: none beyond the common conventions: bucket i = [i*w, (i+1)*w) with w = (max - min)/20 over the original; probabilities divided by the number of trajectories (values outside the buckets stay in the denominator); terms with zero probability skipped (Evaluation.java:513-522)

metrics.name: ada_length_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between travel-distance distributions (sum of consecutive-point distances) over 20 buckets
metrics.adaptation: as ada_diameter_error

metrics.name: ldp_density_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between the cell distributions of all grid-trajectory points (paper Eq. 17)
metrics.source: paper Sec. 6.1.3 (N = 6), 6.2 Eq. 17; main.py:33-38,296-304,377-383; trajectory.py:9-55; utils.py:71-86; parse.py:7
metrics.adaptation: grid trajectories as LDPTrace (consecutive duplicates removed, then diagonal-first interpolation; a trail inside one cell stays one cell); divergence with LDPTrace's +1e-8 smoothing inside the log

metrics.name: ldp_hotspot_error
metrics.statistic: 1 - NDCG@5 of the release's top-5 cells against the original's top-5 (relevance 1/original rank; paper Eq. 19)
metrics.adaptation: cell ties ranked by cell index (Python's stable sort)

metrics.name: ldp_query_error
metrics.statistic: average relative error of 200 square range queries counting points (paper Eq. 18), sanity bound 1% of the original's points
metrics.source: paper Sec. 6.1.3 (r = 1/9 of the space), Eq. 18; main.py:388-396; experiment.py:21-51,85-109; parse.py:9,15
metrics.adaptation: square edge sqrt(W*H/9), centre uniform in the study area (squares may extend beyond it); points are the check-ins themselves (the code queries points re-sampled uniformly inside each grid trajectory's cells, main.py:372, because its releases are grid cells; ours are venue points); release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: ldp_kendall_tau
metrics.statistic: Kendall tau between per-cell numbers of grid trajectories passing through each cell (paper Eq. 20), LDPTrace's tie convention
metrics.adaptation: grid trajectories as ldp_density_error; pairs with tied real counts skipped, release ties count as discordant

metrics.name: ldp_trip_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between (start cell, end cell) distributions
metrics.adaptation: none

metrics.name: ldp_length_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between travel-distance distributions over 20 equal-width buckets
metrics.adaptation: none: bucket i = [i*w, i*w + w] (closed, so values on an edge count twice) with w = (max - min)/20 over the original; each side normalized by its bucket total; a release with an empty histogram scores ln 2

metrics.name: ldp_diameter_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between diameter distributions over 20 equal-width buckets
metrics.adaptation: as ldp_length_error

metrics.name: ldp_pattern_f1
metrics.statistic: F1 of the top-100 patterns (contiguous cell sub-sequences of size 2..8 of the grid trajectories); precision = recall = hits / 100 (paper Eq. 21)
metrics.adaptation: pattern ties broken by key; 0 when there is no hit (the code divides by zero)

metrics.name: ldp_pattern_error
metrics.statistic: sum over the original's top-100 patterns of |n_orig - n_release| / n_orig, divided by 100 (paper Eq. 22)
metrics.adaptation: release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: retra_density_error
metrics.statistic: mean over timestamps of the JSD between the per-timestamp cell distributions of points
metrics.source: paper Sec. V-A (T-Drive: 10-minute timestamps), V-B; evaluation_b.py:115-122; experiment.py:131-135,178-190; parse.py:7 (K = 6)
metrics.adaptation: a timestamp is a 10-minute slot of the week ((t mod 10080) // 10, 1008 slots; T-Drive's granularity); a check-in is a point at its own slot (no carry-forward between check-ins); empty timestamps enter the mean (JSD 0 when both sides are empty), as in the code

metrics.name: retra_transition_error
metrics.statistic: mean over timestamps of the JSD between per-timestamp cell-transition distributions
metrics.adaptation: a transition is a pair of consecutive check-ins of a trail, attributed to the origin's slot; the domain is every cell pair (the code's domain is same-or-adjacent cells because its streams move one cell per timestamp; check-in hops jump); transitions from the last slot are dropped (range(max_time - 1))

metrics.name: retra_query_error
metrics.statistic: average relative error of 100 spatio-temporal range queries (square of 1/9 of the area, phi = 20 consecutive timestamps)
metrics.source: paper Sec. V-B 'Query Error'; evaluation_b.py:104-113,132-170; experiment.py:23-68,110-128; parse.py:14 (phi = 20)
metrics.adaptation: square fully inside the study area (experiment.py:35-36); window start uniform integer in [0, 1008 - phi]; sanity bound 0.01 * upt * phi with upt = original check-ins per timestamp (the code's dataset constant 'average users per timestamp'); release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: retra_pattern_f1
metrics.statistic: mean over 100 random windows of phi = 20 timestamps of the top-100 pattern F1 (patterns of 2..5 consecutive points lying inside the window)
metrics.source: paper Sec. V-B 'Pattern F1'; evaluation_b.py:172-196; experiment.py:71-107,138-175
metrics.adaptation: points are check-in cells (no duplicate removal, no interpolation); a pattern is kept if its first point's slot >= window start and its last point's slot <= window end; patterns of size > 2 with two equal consecutive cells are rejected (Pattern.check_pattern); precision = recall = hits / 100; windows identical to retra_hotspot_ndcg (the code reseeds before both)

metrics.name: retra_kendall_tau
metrics.statistic: Kendall tau of per-cell trajectory coverage, LDPTrace's tie convention
metrics.adaptation: cells of the check-ins (no interpolation); the code splits original streams at non-adjacent moves (evaluation_b.py:36-59,102), which would cut every check-in trail, so trails are not split

metrics.name: retra_length_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between travel-distance distributions over 20 buckets whose range spans BOTH datasets
metrics.adaptation: none: w = (max(max_o, max_r) - min(min_o, min_r)) / 20, closed buckets [i*w, i*w + w]

metrics.name: retra_trip_error
metrics.statistic: JSD between (start cell, end cell) distributions
metrics.adaptation: trails are not split (see retra_kendall_tau)

metrics.name: retra_hotspot_ndcg
metrics.statistic: mean over 100 random windows of phi = 20 timestamps of NDCG@10 of the hotspot cells (relevance 1/original rank)
metrics.source: paper Sec. V-B 'Hotspot NDCG' (n_h = 10); evaluation_b.py:210-244; experiment.py:209-227
metrics.adaptation: windows with no original point are skipped (the code would divide by zero); a release with no point in a window scores 0

metrics.name: priv_length_jsd
metrics.statistic: JSD between travel-distance ('length') distributions over 50 bins
metrics.source: paper Sec. 2.1, 5.1 'Metrics' (50 bins instead of AdaTrace's 20), Appendix B.4
metrics.adaptation: no evaluation code is published: 50 equal-width bins on [0, max of the original]; release values above the maximum go to the last bin

metrics.name: priv_diameter_jsd
metrics.statistic: JSD between diameter distributions over 50 bins
metrics.adaptation: as priv_length_jsd

metrics.name: priv_density_are
metrics.statistic: ARE of 500 random circles with random radius; a query counts the trajectories passing through the circle ('trajectory density')
metrics.source: paper Sec. 5.1 ('random radii' vs AdaTrace's constant radius), Appendix B.4 ARE_TD
metrics.adaptation: unspecified in the source and fixed here: centre uniform in the study area, radius uniform in (0, longer side / 3] (AdaTrace's constant radius as the upper bound), phi = 1% of the original's trajectories (AdaTrace's sanity bound); 'passing through' as ada_query_avre; release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: priv_pattern_are
metrics.statistic: ARE of the top-200 transition patterns (2..5 consecutive states on a 20 x 20 grid) by number of occurrences
metrics.source: paper Sec. 5.1 (20 x 20 grid), Appendix B.4 ARE_TP (mu = 200, patterns of 2 to 5 states), Appendix B.2 (state sequences)
metrics.adaptation: state sequence = cells of the check-ins with consecutive duplicates removed (Appendix B.2); phi = 1% of the original's trajectories (unspecified in the source); ties broken by key; release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: hrnet_waypoint
metrics.statistic: for each of the original's 30 most frequent start cells, the mean over all cells l of the JSD between Bernoulli(Pr(l in v[1:] | v0 = start)) of the two datasets, averaged over the start cells
metrics.source: arXiv 2405.08043v2 Appendix A.3 Eq. 10 and A.3.1 (|L_start| = 30, binary support); Table 1 (w = 32); evaluation.py:602-612 (count_route_locations: set(traj[1:]) minus the start); evaluation.py:421-489 (compute_divergence, uniform fallback when the release has no trajectory from a start)
metrics.adaptation: POIs are the 32 x 32 grid cells of the check-ins (HRNet's POIs are grid cells); waypoints are the check-ins (stay points); the mean over cells follows the appendix formula (HRNet's published numbers are the sum over cells, a constant factor)

metrics.name: hrnet_destination
metrics.statistic: mean over the 30 start cells of the JSD between Pr(v[-1] = l | v0 = start)
metrics.adaptation: as hrnet_waypoint; a release with no trajectory from a start cell is scored against the uniform distribution (compute_divergence)

metrics.name: hrnet_transition
metrics.statistic: mean over the 30 start cells of the JSD between Pr(v[1] = l | v0 = start)
metrics.adaptation: as hrnet_destination

metrics.name: hrnet_travel_distance
metrics.statistic: JSD between travel-distance distributions over n_bin = 30 ranges of [0, d_max]
metrics.adaptation: d_max = maximum of the original; release values above it go to the last range (Eq. 13's ranges end at d_max)

metrics.name: hrnet_diameter
metrics.statistic: JSD between diameter distributions over 30 ranges of [0, d_max]
metrics.adaptation: as hrnet_travel_distance

metrics.name: hrnet_density_t
metrics.statistic: mean over discrete times t of the JSD between Pr(v[i] = l | t[i] <= t < t[i+1]) (where trajectories are at time t)
metrics.adaptation: discrete times are the 168 hour boundaries of the week; a trail is at the cell of its latest check-in between two check-ins (half-open [t_i, t_{i+1}) instead of the formula's open interval, so check-ins on the hour are not lost); only times at which the original has a trajectory enter the mean; a release with none there is scored against the uniform distribution

metrics.name: hrnet_traj_density
metrics.statistic: ARE of 500 random POI sets: the number of trajectories visiting at least one POI of the set
metrics.adaptation: unspecified in the source and fixed here: set size uniform in {1, ..., 1024} cells, cells drawn without replacement; phi = 1% of the original's trajectories; release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: hrnet_traj_pattern
metrics.statistic: ARE over the original's top-200 patterns longer than 2 of the number of trajectories containing each pattern
metrics.adaptation: contiguous cell sub-sequences of the check-ins (no duplicate removal); length capped at 5 (PrivTrace's bound; the source gives none); phi = 1% of the original's trajectories; ties broken by key; release counts rescaled by s

metrics.name: movesim_distance
metrics.statistic: JSD between the distributions of squared distances between consecutive locations over 10000 equal-width bins
metrics.source: paper Sec. 4.2 'Distance'; evaluations.py:193-202,286-293 (get_distances returns dx^2 + dy^2), 40-54, 90-104
metrics.adaptation: consecutive check-ins instead of consecutive half-hour slots; the code's histogram range for SQUARED distances is the dataset constant max_distance (unsquared, evaluations.py:290-292) while the radius histogram uses max_distance^2 (299-301); we use D^2 for both, D = study-area diagonal (km), so the range does not depend on the unit; edges np.arange(0, D^2, D^2/10000) as in the code

metrics.name: movesim_radius
metrics.statistic: JSD between the distributions of the squared radius of gyration (mean squared distance to the trajectory's centre) over 10000 bins
metrics.adaptation: range [0, D^2) with D = study-area diagonal (km); per trail instead of per user-day

metrics.name: movesim_duration
metrics.statistic: JSD between stay-duration distributions (48 bins of half an hour over one day)
metrics.adaptation: a stay is a maximal run of consecutive check-ins at the same venue; its duration is the time to the next check-in at another venue, in days (the code counts consecutive half-hour slots at the same location); the last stay of every trail is dropped, as in the code; edges np.arange(0, 1, 1/48)

metrics.name: movesim_dailyloc
metrics.statistic: JSD between the distributions of the number of distinct locations per trajectory (divided by 48, 48 bins)
metrics.adaptation: distinct venues per trail (trails last at most a day; no user ids, so a trail stands for MoveSim's user-day)

metrics.name: movesim_grank
metrics.statistic: JSD between the histograms (100 bins on [0, 1)) of the visit probabilities of the 100 most visited locations
metrics.adaptation: locations are catalog venues; visit probabilities over all catalog venues

metrics.name: movesim_irank
metrics.statistic: JSD between the histograms (100 bins on [0, 1)) of the normalized mean visit frequencies of each trajectory's 1st..100th most visited location
metrics.adaptation: the individual is the trail (no user ids; each MoveSim trajectory is also one user-day), so I-rank is computable

metrics.name: movesim_grank_rank
metrics.statistic: JSD between the two top-100 visit-probability profiles as distributions over ranks 1..100 (the paper's wording, without the code's histogram of values)
metrics.adaptation: variant: reported, excluded from headline counts. With 10^4-10^6 catalog venues every top-100 probability is far below the code's first bin (0.01), which collapses movesim_grank

metrics.name: movesim_irank_rank
metrics.statistic: JSD between the mean per-trajectory rank-frequency profiles over ranks 1..100
metrics.adaptation: variant of movesim_irank without the code's histogram of values

metrics.name: llmob_sd
metrics.statistic: JSD between step-distance distributions (distance between consecutive locations): 10 bins of 1 km on [0, 10] plus one overflow bin
metrics.adaptation: projected km instead of haversine (difference < 0.5% inside a city); distances rounded to 3 decimals as in geodistance

metrics.name: llmob_si
metrics.statistic: JSD between step-interval distributions (time between consecutive check-ins on 10-minute slots): 12 bins of 1 hour on [0, 12] plus one overflow bin
metrics.adaptation: the code applies its 12 unit-width bins to MINUTES (duration() multiplies slot differences by 10), which puts every interval of 20 minutes or more into the overflow bin; we apply them to hours; the literal minute version is llmob_si_code

metrics.name: llmob_si_code
metrics.statistic: llmob_si with the code's literal minute unit
metrics.adaptation: variant: reported, excluded from headline counts

metrics.name: llmob_dard
metrics.statistic: JSD between the histograms of (10-minute interval of the day, activity category) tuples of all check-ins
metrics.source: paper Sec. 4.1 (3) ('a histogram is then constructed to represent the distribution of the collected tuples'); evaluate.py:193-218
metrics.adaptation: activity category = FSQ root category of the venue (LLMob uses the 10 Foursquare top-level categories); the exact tuple histogram (the code maps tuples to first-appearance ids quantized into 1000 bins, which equals the tuple histogram only when at most 1001 distinct tuples occur; here 144 x 11 can); the code version is llmob_dard_code

metrics.name: llmob_dard_code
metrics.statistic: llmob_dard with the code's quantization: tuple ids normalized to [0, 1] and histogrammed into 1000 bins plus overflow
metrics.adaptation: variant; ids follow the sorted tuple order (the code's first-appearance order depends on file row order)

metrics.name: llmob_stvd
metrics.statistic: JSD between the histograms of (10-minute interval of the day, location) tuples of all check-ins
metrics.adaptation: a location is a catalog venue (one coordinate pair each); the exact tuple histogram; the code version (400 bins) is llmob_stvd_code

metrics.name: llmob_stvd_code
metrics.statistic: llmob_stvd with the code's quantization of sorted tuple ids into 400 bins plus overflow
metrics.adaptation: variant; ids follow the sorted (slot, venue) order

next_poi.source: Massive-STEPS README.md:63 ('each trajectory will be treated as a sequence of POIs and the last POI will be the target next POI'); src/run_next_poi_llm.py:32-40 (Acc@1, Acc@5, NDCG@5); GETNext fork utils.py:99-180 (Acc@k, NDCG@k, MRR at the last timestep)
next_poi.task: train a next-POI model on the release, evaluate on the real test split (downstream/train_eval.py protocol v2.1: closed vocabulary of the training venues, out-of-vocabulary targets are misses, early stopping on real val, expected rank under random tie-breaking)

scopes.last: primary: the last check-in of each real test trail given all earlier ones (Massive-STEPS)
scopes.all: variant: every position k >= 1 (the project's protocol v2.1)

next_poi.adaptation: no user ids or user history (trail-level releases); candidates are the release's venues, not every POI

statistics.cell: a (dataset, epsilon, metric) combination; methods are compared on seed means; reference = real train
statistics.per_cell: Welch t-test (two-sided) between the seed values of TrajPE and each baseline; significant win/loss at p < 0.05, otherwise tie; cells with fewer than 2 seeds on either side are compared by mean only and reported as such
statistics.raw_counts: win/loss/tie of TrajPE vs each baseline by seed mean (tie = equal within 1e-12 relative)
statistics.loss: lower-is-better metrics: the value; higher-is-better: 1 - value (Kendall tau: 1 - tau in [0, 2])
statistics.normalized_difference: d = (loss_baseline - loss_TrajPE) / (loss_baseline + loss_TrajPE) in [-1, 1] (0 when both are 0); d > 0 means TrajPE is better
statistics.across_cells: per baseline over all cells both methods have: Wilcoxon signed-rank test on d (two-sided, zero differences dropped) and sign test (two-sided binomial on the signs); Holm correction over baselines
statistics.ranks: per cell, methods ranked by loss (ties get average ranks); average rank per method over the cells where every method is present; Friedman test; Nemenyi critical difference CD = q_0.05(k, inf) / sqrt(2) * sqrt(k (k + 1) / (6 N))
statistics.headline: primary metrics only, each statistic once (ldp_trip_error and retra_trip_error equal ada_trip_error up to the 1e-8 smoothing and are excluded); variants and duplicates are reported in the full tables
statistics.measured_split: the same tables restricted to the metrics TrajPE v3 does not measure directly (see v3_split), reported separately

v3_split.purpose: separate the protocol metrics whose statistic TrajPE v3 measures directly with a DP histogram (and may therefore be calibrated to) from the held-out ones
v3_split.v3_measurements: the workload families of the v3 config (work_families, see trajpe/workload.py) plus the five steering marginals of trajpe/marginals.py (start, cat, venue, cat_trans, venue_trans), which v3 always releases
rule: measured: some unrestricted v3 measurement has the metric's unit and its variables include the metric's (after closure), at any resolution and per-trail weighting

near: not measured, but measured after relaxing the unit (gridpoint -> checkin, coverage -> checkin, stay -> hop) and the variables (distinct -> length, stay_duration -> gap), or the metric's variables are covered jointly by several measurements of its unit (restricted ones included)
unmeasured: otherwise; next-POI metrics are tasks and always unmeasured

cat_trans.restricted: top-200 categories of the DP category marginal (marginals.TOP_CATEGORIES)

venue_trans.restricted: top-500 venues of the DP venue marginal (marginals.TOP_VENUES)
